howToPlaySub: Read the instructions below before starting your assessment.
step1Body: Each question presents a waste item in a clinical context. Identify which of the four bins it belongs in.
step2BodyTouch: Press and hold the item card, then drag it onto the correct colored bin below. Release to drop.
step2BodyDesktop: Drag the item card into the correct bin, or simply click the bin directly.
step3Body: You have 20 seconds per question. Answering faster earns more bonus points on top of the base 100.
landingHeroSub: Interactive, WHO-based medical waste sorting assessment. Drag items into the correct bin — race against the clock and earn your certificate.
readFirstSub: Learn about the 4 waste categories before the test
takeTestSub: Jump straight in — 10 questions, 20 sec each
medicalWasteGuideSub: Based on WHO Healthcare Waste Management Guidelines. Read through the four waste categories, their examples, and disposal rules before taking the assessment.
cat_general_desc: General waste makes up the majority of healthcare waste — roughly 75–90%. It includes items that have not come into contact with blood, body fluids, or hazardous chemicals. This waste is treated the same as municipal solid waste.
cat_general_rules: No sharps or meds in this bin
cat_general_ref: WHO Guidelines Ch. 4 — Non-hazardous Healthcare Waste
cat_infectious_desc: Infectious waste poses a biological risk. It includes anything contaminated with blood, body fluids, secretions, or excretions, as well as materials from isolation wards.
cat_sharps_desc: Sharps are extremely hazardous. Even if sterile, they are classified as hazardous because they cause injury and potential secondary infection.
cat_pharmaceutical_desc: Includes drugs and vaccines that are expired, unused, or contaminated. Improper disposal can contaminate water and contribute to drug resistance.
principle1_body: Waste must be sorted at the exact point of generation. Never mix categories after the fact.
principle2_body: Colors are regulatory requirements: Black (General), Yellow (Infectious), Red (Sharps), Blue (Meds).
principle3_body: Place sharps in containers immediately after use. Never recap needles using two hands.
principle4_title: When in Doubt, Treat as Infectious
principle4_body: If unsure, default to the yellow bin. Over-segregation is safer than under-segregation.
